text: Vets do the medicine, so their Scout is built around visits, records and prescriptions. Here's what they see, and what a relief vet doesn't.
The one thing to remember: a vet needs the Veterinarian role at their office and a veterinary license. The role opens the screens; the license lets them sign and prescribe.
This is Dr. Ortiz, a staff veterinarian. Home, Scheduling, Catalog, Pharmacy, Labs, Tasks and Settings.
Vets see the services they delivered: their own production,
vets manage the clinical setup they own, like euthanasia consent and aftercare.
a vet can void a payment on their own visits.
Now Dr. Park, a relief vet. The same clinical screens, but no Settings in the top bar.
If he opens Settings anyway, Scout says so: none of his roles includes a Settings permission.
His Analytics has only inventory: no production or finance reports.
On a visit, a relief vet examines, writes and signs records and prescribes, just like a staff vet. He can't void payments, see controlled-drug reports, or manage tasks for others.
The most common mistake is giving a new vet the role but not the license, or the license but no office.
Remember: a vet needs the Veterinarian role at their office, and a veterinary license.
